issues.detail: The Greek 'οπτασιαν αγγελων' refers to a 'vision of angels' (the vision itself), but the Vietnamese 'sự hiện thấy của các thiên sứ' can be interpreted as 'the appearance/presence of the angels' rather than a visionary experience. More importantly, the Greek structure 'εωρακεναι οι λεγουσιν αυτον ζην' indicates that the people *who were saying* He was alive were the ones who had seen the vision. The Vietnamese phrasing 'những người nói Ngài đang sống' is placed at the end of the sentence as a non-restrictive description, potentially losing the grammatical link that identifies them specifically as the ones who saw the vision.
